- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot.
- In periods with high sentiment volatility (alternating +/– > 0.5), model fails to smooth transitions; use moving average of last 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume mean reversion; reduce next forecast by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; weight final 5–7 days of history more heavily in smoothing.
